correctness.rationale: For \(D(t)=|1+e^{it}-e^{3it}|^3-|1+e^{it}+e^{3it}|^3\), the submitted derivative estimate gives \(\|D''\|_1\le2232\pi\): for either trinomial, \(|P|\le3\), \(|P'|\le4\), \(|P''|\le10\), and the Hessian formula for \(|P|^3\) yields the pointwise 558 bound, extending through zeros because \((x^2+y^2)^{3/2}\) is \(C^2\). Two integrations by parts and root-of-unity aliasing therefore give \(|\Delta_L-I|\le372\pi^2/L^2\) for the continuous mean I. The inspected directed-interval verifier certifies \(\Delta_{10000}\) near 0.1155409795794836083, hence \(I>0.1155042646511115\) and the tail \(L\ge200\) exceeds 0.0237169437209805. It separately certifies every \(5\le L\le199\), with minimum lower endpoint at \(L=10\) above 0.1055728090. The exact low-order formulas are negative for L=1,2,3,4. Thus the finite interval work plus analytic aliasing covers all L; no finite enumeration is extrapolated to infinity.
correctness.risk: The numerical certificates depend on directed interval arithmetic as carried in the inspected verifier; the analytic tail constant has ample margin relative to 0.0237.

final_claim: For \(\Delta_L=L^{-1}\sum_{j=0}^{L-1}(|1+\omega_L^j-\omega_L^{3j}|^3-|1+\omega_L^j+\omega_L^{3j}|^3)\), one has \(\Delta_L<0\) for \(1\le L\le4\), while \(\Delta_L>0\) for every \(L\ge5\), in fact \(\Delta_L>0.0237\) uniformly for all \(L\ge5\).
limitations: The theorem does not address other exponents or arbitrary three-term frequency sets.
